object_types.name: Patient
object_types.definition: A person who receives medical care at the clinic and books appointments.

object_types.name: Doctor

ambiguities.description: Scheduling uniqueness across multiple dimensions not fully specified. The transcript mentions appointments are booked with a date and time slot, but does not explicitly state whether a doctor can have multiple appointments on the same date-time combination, or whether the date-time combination uniquely identifies an appointment within an exam room context. Are there business rules like 'a doctor can have at most one appointment per date-time' or 'an exam room can be occupied by at most one appointment per date-time'?

source_references.excerpt: Every appointment is on a date and at a time slot -- we book in fixed slots like 09:00 or 09:30.

ambiguities.description: Exam room assignment not captured. The transcript mentions that exam rooms have a room number (line 11), but does not describe how exam rooms relate to appointments. Are appointments assigned to exam rooms? If so, is this relationship mandatory, and can an exam room have multiple appointments across different time slots?

source_references.excerpt: Exam rooms have a room number.

ambiguities.description: Primary doctor and appointment doctor relationship. The transcript states that every patient has exactly one primary doctor (line 31), and each appointment is with exactly one doctor (line 7). However, it does not clarify whether the doctor in a given appointment must be the patient's primary doctor, can be any doctor, or has some other constraint. Are there cases where a patient sees a doctor other than their primary?

source_references.excerpt: Each appointment is with exactly one doctor. Doctors see many patients across their appointments.
Yes, every patient has exactly one primary doctor. That's separate from who they happen to see in a given appointment.

ambiguities.description: Visit reason and follow-up note cardinality. Line 27 states that an appointment 'can have' a visit reason and 'can attach' a follow-up note, indicating optionality. However, the inverse direction is not specified: must every visit reason be associated with an appointment, and must every follow-up note be attached to an appointment? These are typically mandatory on the value side, but this should be confirmed.

source_references.excerpt: An appointment can have a visit reason the patient gives when booking, and after the visit the doctor can attach a follow-up note. At most one follow-up note per appointment.

ambiguities.description: Specialty optionality and uniqueness. The transcript states every doctor has exactly one specialty, but does not clarify whether multiple doctors can have the same specialty. For example, can two doctors both have cardiology as their specialty? Also, is the specialty a free-text value or restricted to a predefined list of specialties?

source_references.excerpt: Every doctor has exactly one specialty, like cardiology or general practice.
